findings.reason: the section must add this sixth cascade to its census, retire pick_input_cache_root onto the new owner (or exempt it with a reason), and correct the "retired resolvers were private" accounting, since leaving a home-first cascade unfound is the exact reuse gap the plan exists to close.
findings.text: §13 measures "five cache cascades in two deliberate orders" but reckon/capabilities.py:1143 pick_input_cache_root is a sixth cascade, RECKON_HOME-then-XDG_CACHE_HOME (home first, lines 1158-1164), which is public and drives the ledger's sqlite path at reckon/ledger.py:791; a scenario this changes: §13's done-when `grep -rn 'XDG_CACHE_HOME' reckon/` reports the cascade in exactly one function, which cannot be satisfied while this resolver keeps its own XDG_CACHE_HOME read, yet the section neither lists it among the five, counts its public definition, nor names it for consolidation

findings.reason: the section's goal is one home that hides the ordering; resolving home_step from a kind-keyed table inside cache_root removes the knob and makes the order a property of the kind rather than of the caller.
findings.text: the interface `cache_root(kind, *, home_step)` takes the cascade's ordering as a caller-supplied argument with three values (home before XDG, home after XDG, no home), but the section's own description fixes one order per kind (velocity and the detector after XDG, run-time-profile and lane-context before XDG, the served client cache with none), so home_step is a function of kind and every call site must restate it; a scenario this changes: a fifth kind added later copies whichever home_step a neighbour's call site happens to show rather than inheriting its kind's order, and nothing at the interface makes a wrong order visible

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — the proposed cache_root(kind, *, home_step) on reckon/velocity.py exports the cascade's internal ordering as a required call-site parameter, so five callers must each restate where the reckon home enters instead of the interface hiding it.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the cascade census in §13 is one short: reckon/capabilities.py:1143 pick_input_cache_root is a sixth cascade, public, home-first, and the owner to extend and the accounting to correct.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1476, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §12 states net zero (one public reader on velocity added, public revised_python retired) and §13 states +2 (the process runner and cache_root), with no CLI option, MCP view or refusal family added, and the arithmetic is consistent with the supplied public_definitions count.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — §12/§13 name and open the machinery they touch (velocity.git and read_blobs, routing._git, clones._git and revised_python, interface_counts.read_trees, and the capabilities/lane_context/serve cascades), and §2–§11 each cite the census or owner they replace; the one mechanism the search missed is filed under duplicate_owner.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the two retained wrappers are each justified in the section text: velocity.git keeps its bytes-and-raise contract over the new runner, and routing._git stays as error-domain translation into CrewError rather than a second runner.
